chunks: he used to forbid women from examining themselves regarding menstruation (haydh) at night, and he would say: 'Indeed, it may turn out to be yellowness (sufra) or turbidity (kudra).'

key_terms.الصُّفْرَة: sufra — yellowish discharge that may appear around the time of menstruation
key_terms.الْكُدْرَة: kudra — turbid or murky discharge, also of uncertain menstrual status
key_terms.الْمَحِيض: haydh — menstruation; the state of ritual impurity with specific rulings

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about women examining themselves for menstruation at night?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a practical ruling prohibiting women from checking their menstrual status at night. The reasoning is that in low-light conditions, post-menstrual yellowish discharge (sufra) or murky discharge (kudra) could be mistaken for active menstrual blood, leading to an incorrect determination of one's state of ritual purity (tahara) and thus affecting the validity of prayer and other acts of worship. This hadith reflects the Imam's careful attention to conditions that may cause errors in fiqh rulings.
word_analysis: it is / it turns out to be
